anchors.description: Length of the right-hand single/twin bed along its visible near top edge, from the head-end corner at the back wall to the foot-end corner where the bedspread folds down.
anchors.visible_evidence: Both points lie on the visible mattress top surface: the head-left corner at the wall below the pillow, and the foot-left corner where the polka-dot spread turns over the end; the full length of the bed is traceable along this taut top edge.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Standard narrow bed; on-screen length/width ratio (~2.2) strongly favors twin (0.97 m wide) over full/double (1.37 m), but twin (1.905 m) vs twin-XL (2.03 m) cannot be distinguished, hence the interval.

anchors.description: Long front edge of the white pillow lying at the head of the right bed, from its lower-left corner to its lower-right corner.
anchors.visible_evidence: The pillow's bright white top/front face and its long lower edge are clearly visible against the grey bedspread, with both end corners resolvable.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Standard US pillow 20x26 in (0.51x0.66 m); queen 20x30 (0.76 m) and king 20x36 (0.91 m) are possible, but the pillow measures ~0.70 of the bed width, consistent with the 26 in length, so the interval is kept tight around standard/queen-small.

anchors.description: Vertical distance on the back wall from the underside of the window sill to the wall/floor junction directly below it.
anchors.visible_evidence: The window's bottom sill/trim line and, directly beneath it, the white baseboard and hardwood floor line where the back wall meets the floor are both plainly visible at the same image column.
anchors.identity_uncertainty: Residential window sill height above finished floor is commonly 30-36 in (0.76-0.91 m), but construction varies; the window is cut by the top of the frame so its own height cannot pin the scale, hence the wide interval.
